latest_release.body:
<!-- flclash:changelog:begin -->
### Features
- **about** Icons and even spacing for the update settings on the About page
- **window** Pause live updates on desktop while the screen is asleep or locked
- **update** Install macOS updates from inside the app
- **proxies** Proxy groups unfold smoothly as one block
- **connection** Connection, request, DNS, outbound IP and log details use smaller text with more room
- **prism_ui** List rows follow a smaller text size, as they already did a larger one
- **prism_ui** The phone tab bar spaces five tabs and sets out icons and labels as iOS does
- **about** The automatic update check and the update channel moved from General settings to the About page
- **logs** Filter logs from a button beside search
- **logs** Set the log level from the Logs page
- **requests** Connections become Requests: connections by minute with All, Active and Failed counts, conditions on app, exit, rule or protocol, a timeline for each connection, DNS queries, segments that keep their place, and new rows held under a desktop pointer
- **update** Choose between stable and prerelease updates in the settings; the prerelease check finds the newest release and names the installed prerelease
- **ui** Lists and cards share one set of margins, so rows line up across pages
- **dashboard** The dashboard's outbound mode card is titled Outbound, leaving its mode buttons more room
- **ui** Grouped lists match iOS 27: row heights, margins, corners and section spacing
- **logs** On desktop, Logs moves from the sidebar into Tools
- **connections** Connections on macOS, Windows and Linux show the icon of the app that made them
- **navigation** Requests sits right after Proxies in the desktop sidebar
- **connections** Connections that failed to connect now show in the requests list, with the reason
- **update** When an update has no file to download, the app opens the release page to download it by hand

### Bug Fixes
- **proxies** A rounder, larger delay test icon on proxy cards
- **prism_ui** Navigation bar tabs fit their titles, and a tap near a tab's edge selects it
- **dashboard** Live connections on the dashboard open on the active ones
- **rules** The rule type picker and rule lists show rule types as profiles write them, such as DOMAIN-KEYWORD, and rule search finds a rule by that name
- **core** A stop whose answer is lost with the connection to the core no longer turns the proxy back on when the core comes back
- **setup** Restarting the core with TUN on no longer hangs when it has to ask for authorization again
- **core** On desktop, a restart asked for while the core is still starting, such as after installing the helper, now restarts it, and the core can start again after a start whose local connection setup hung
- **core** On Android, stopping while the core is still starting no longer leaves it running, and a start that failed while sending settings to the core no longer blocks the next start
- **probes** Recheck watched service failures with backoff
- **probes** Service checks recover automatically when a chain switches to a working front proxy
- **setup** Dashboard checks wait for startup to finish when you tap Start as the app opens
- **l10n** Shorter descriptions in network, DNS and general settings
- **segmented-control** Segmented controls follow the system's reduce motion setting
- **connected-button** Screen readers can now switch the dashboard's outbound mode
- **scaffold** On wider phones the top bar buttons line up with the list cards below them
- **scaffold** Opening search puts the cursor in its field even when something else on the page has the focus
- **android** App icons in access control and connections load from the cache instead of being redrawn every day
- **core** On macOS, connections show the app that opened them again
- **window** A hidden window no longer takes the foreground from a full-screen game on Windows
- **linux** The Linux window is no longer drawn shifted toward the bottom left

detail.readme:
# FlClash A multi-platform proxy client based on ClashMeta. Simple to use, open source and ad-free. **English** · [简体中文](README_zh_CN.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/chen08209/FlClash?style=flat-square&label=release)](https://github.com/chen08209/FlClash/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/chen08209/FlClash/total?style=flat-square&logo=github)](https://github.com/chen08209/FlClash/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/chen08209/FlClash?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Telegram](https://img.shields.io/badge/Telegram-channel-26A5E4?style=flat-square&logo=telegram&logoColor=white)](https://t.me/FlClash) [Website](https://chen08209.github.io/FlClash) · [Download](#download) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Build from source](#build-from-source)

## Features - **One app for Android, Windows, macOS and Linux**, with x64 and ARM64 builds on the desktop. - **mihomo (Clash.Meta) core** with rule routing, proxy groups, latency tests, system proxy and TUN mode. - **Profiles** from a subscription link or a file, with a built-in editor, override scripts, and custom rules, proxies and proxy groups. - **Live views** of connections, requests, DNS queries and logs. - **Material You design with Apple-style interaction**: dynamic color, light and dark themes, continuous corners, sheets that snap between heights, and layouts that adapt from phones to desktops. - **Backup and restore** through WebDAV or a local file. - **Platform touches**: a Quick Settings tile, per-app proxy and Android TV support on Android; a tray menu and global hotkeys on the desktop. - **Open source and ad-free**, licensed under GPL-3.0. ## Download Get the latest build from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/chen08209/FlClash/releases/latest), or open the [website](https://chen08209.github.io/FlClash#download), which picks the right file for your device. | Platform | Packages | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Android | APK for `arm64` (arm64-v8a), `armv7` (armeabi-v7a) and `amd64` (x86_64) | Most phones use `arm64`. Also on the F-Droid repository below. | | Windows 10 and later | Installer (`.exe`) or portable `.zip`, for x64 and ARM64 | Pick ARM64 on Snapdragon and other ARM laptops. | | macOS 12 and later | DMG for Apple Silicon and Intel | Also on Homebrew. | | Linux | `.deb`, `.rpm` and AppImage, for x64 and ARM64 | See the tray note below. |

**Homebrew** ```bash brew tap chen08209/tap brew install --cask flclash ``` **macOS first launch** The app is not notarized, so macOS refuses to open it the first time. After dragging it to Applications, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FlClash*.app`, or choose Open Anyway under System Settings > Privacy & Security. Later updates install from inside the app. **Linux tray icon** The tray icon is a StatusNotifierItem. KDE Plasma, XFCE and most panels show it as is; GNOME needs the AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support extension. **Unattended desktop** FlClash starts the core only after the disclaimer is accepted. Where nobody can click it, such as a container, set `FLCLASH_ACCEPT_DISCLAIMER=1` in the app's environment to accept it on first launch. ## Usage **Import a profile from a link.** Opening a link in this form imports the subscription into FlClash. The `clashmeta://` and `flclash://` schemes work the same way. ```text clash://install-config?url= ``` **Automate on Android.** Tasker, MacroDroid and similar apps can start, stop or toggle the proxy by starting an activity with one of these actions: ```text com.follow.clash.action.START com.follow.clash.action.STOP com.follow.clash.action.TOGGLE ``` From a computer, the same works over adb: ```bash adb shell am start -a com.follow.clash.action.TOGGLE ``` ## Build from source You need [Flutter](https://docs.flutter.dev/get-started/install) 3.50 (release builds use 3.50.1), [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) 1.27 and [Rust](https://rustup.rs/) installed through rustup. Each platform builds on its own host, except Android, which builds anywhere. ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/chen08209/FlClash.git cd FlClash flutter pub get dart run tool/package.dart android # or windows, macos, linux ``` Packages land in `dist/`. The Go core and the Rust libraries are compiled as part of the Flutter build. | Platform | Also needed | | --- | --- | | Android | Android SDK with the NDK. Add `--arch arm64` to build a single ABI. | | Windows | GCC (MinGW-w64) for the core and [Inno Setup](https://jrsoftware.org/isinfo.php) 6 for the installer. | | macOS | Xcode and Node.js. The script installs `appdmg` through npm. | | Linux | Debian or Ubuntu. The script installs the build packages with apt and downloads `appimagetool`. | Run `dart run tool/package.dart --help` for the remaining options, such as `--targets` to build only some package formats or `--dry-run` to list the files a run would write. ## Support Starring the repository is the easiest way to support the project. Questions and announcements go to the [Telegram channel](https://t.me/FlClash); bugs and feature requests go to [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/chen08209/FlClash/issues). ## License FlClash is released under the [GPL-3.0 license](LICENSE).
